root_cause.text: In `mm/vmalloc.c`’s `vrealloc_node_align_noprof()`, the realloc path could allocate a smaller `size` buffer but still `memcpy()` the full `old_size` into it, causing an out-of-bounds write when shrinking and a NUMA/alignment-triggered reallocation occurs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(n, p, old_size);` to `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size));`, and the CVE description states that on the `need_realloc` path the code “allocates a new object of 'size' bytes and then memcpy()s 'old_size' bytes into it,” which overflows when `size < old_size`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `vrealloc_node_align_noprof()` to copy only the valid amount of data when reallocating, especially when the allocation is reduced in size.
intent_record.what: The memcpy call in `vrealloc_node_align_noprof()` was changed from copying `old_size` bytes to copying `min(size, old_size)` bytes before freeing the old allocation.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from copying more data than the newly requested allocation size can hold when shrinking a block, avoiding an out-of-bounds write during reallocation while preserving the existing contents up to the smaller of the old and new sizes.

grouping_result.intent: Fix `vrealloc_node_align_noprof()` to copy only the valid amount of data when reallocating, especially when the allocation is reduced in size.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes vrealloc_node_align_noprof() so realloc only copies the valid amount of data instead of the full old_size, preventing the out-of-bounds write when shrinking.

candidates.rationale: This copies the entire old allocation size into the newly allocated buffer even when the new buffer is smaller, directly causing an out-of-bounds write during realloc/shrink cases.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies the full old allocation size into the newly allocated buffer even when the realloc path has produced a smaller buffer, which can overflow the destination during shrink/reallocation cases.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is a realloc path that allocates a smaller `size` buffer but still copies `old_size` bytes into it, causing an out-of-bounds write during shrink/NUMA-alignment reallocation. In this snippet, that unsafe pattern is not present: the only copy is in the ზრდing path, `if (p) { memcpy(n, p, old_size); vfree(p); }`, and it happens only after `n = __vmalloc_noprof(size, flags);` where `size > old_size` due to the preceding `if (size <= old_size) { ... return (void *)p; }`. The shrink case returns the original pointer without allocating a smaller buffer, so the bug condition is absent. The code also already contains the relevant fix behavior by preserving contents only up to the lesser of new and old sizes: `if (size <= old_size) { ... return (void *)p; }` and `memcpy(n, p, old_size)` only on growth, so the vulnerable OOB write is prevented in this implementation.
